institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Was my 3rd option, but I picked it because i knew very little of Austria and Vienna, but knew some german beforehand. Also crucial that the institution already had an agreement with my home University.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Fun, but also alot of paper-work to make things work. However, I feel that because I put in alot of work, to find courses, to make my exchange better and so on, it actually became better. Workload was light and courses was interesting.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I feel like I was either bombarded with information, or left alone to figure things out myself. E.g. language requirements, which mattered, and then it didn't really matter, and then I had to do an expensive high-level-language exam with only one weeks notice. But in the end it didn't matter at all again. Confusing to say the least. This properly also overshadowed my feeling towards my the whole thing before I went on exchange, because I thought many times that my exchange would fail, before I even went. I think other than that it was good and informative.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was greeted very well, and I felt like I knew where to go and what to do. Also being linked up with other students was good ! Although, their system with courses was confusing and took alot of time to figure out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was extremely lucky to find my housing. Made an Instagram Story, and found my room in just one day after posting. A friend of a friend had a cheap room 20 min by foot from campus. 

I would definately recommend this, as an option, because maybe someone knows someone - And this is deffinetly the best way if you want to have a more "local" feeling.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Campus is on the top of a hill, and biking there was very annoying - especially coming from flat Denmark - however I learned to love walking more. Other than that, I feel that living off campus was pretty chill. I lived between the busy city centre and UNI campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I never looked at the things made available for students, since I found it so early myself

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy but course registration was confusing, and it takes a loooong time to figure out what is good, fun, etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty easy I would say. I was told where to be and when, where to sign and what. It took some time to get used to a new system, but when you know, you know

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was put in connection with a uni-buddy, but I never really used her help, because of the 2 people i lived with also studied at same uni. So they became my main source of help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all courses I wanted, however it is good to be out in good time. Courses fill up fast, especially the fun ones

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I did german courses and alot of courses with excursions involved. This is what made my workload abit lighter and more fun. 

Also signing up for sports at the USI (Wien sport uni) was really good. I did boxing for a few weeks and badminton the whole semester. Sign up fast, when they open for signing up!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I feel like I did courses that weren't that connected directly to landscape architecture, but more around it. This was also very cool and insightful to try something new.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Very difficult to only find BA courses in english that are related to my studies. However it is also possible to find MA courses that also start from scratch. 

However I also spend alot of time looking into the the levels and requirements of the courses I signed up for.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less personal. Felt more official. Also absense was noted and in some courses almost everything was being taken into account for my final grade which was abit terrifying. In the begining I was scared of doing things wrong.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
OEKB001374 Biodiversity, what is it good for?

AGRI302083 Case studies in organic grassland management

OEKB001324 (Eco-) tourism & management of protected areas

WISO100324 Environmental and energy policy in the EU

120016 German for Science (BOKU specific topics) - Course A (B2+)

WISO300579 Globalisation and rural development

120004 Intensive German Refresher Course - moderate advanced

LAWI301432 Sketching

WISO100323 Social ecology: Sustainability of society-nature interactions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sketching ! one week of drawing in innercity. no exams, no requirements.

Case studies in organic grassland management - 2 days at a organic farm in the alps. 

Biodiversity, what is it good for? - Fun profs that just argue

(Eco-) tourism & management of protected areas - Confusing in the beginning because it was a very different way of learning than what im used to, but we ended the course with a rafting-boat tour down the Donau.

In general all very good courses, with minimal workload but still very insightful and fun. - Also no exams

Globalisation and rural development, was abit boring and had a written exam

questions.answer: I bought zero books

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again sign up for USI. and look into the student cafe/bar for events

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds ! USI sport. Clubs, events through the exchange group or uni cafe

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend taking advantage of the location of Vienna. Many cool and beautiful cities very close by.

Do alot of walking and hikes ! Ride a bike in the hills around Vienna.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do atleast one museum ! my favorite is the national art gallery. then go to cafes, heurigers (local wine taverns). stand at Heldenplatz at night or daytime and look around. you'll be amazed by the architecture around you.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy I would say

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: USI, Uni-bar

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: . In general a bit more conservative and old-fashioned vibe in the general public, but it was never really a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cafe culture, and the appreciation of old things. Renovations are not always good !

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Figure out the language requirements for uni

Spend time on looking in to courses - its worth it in the end (however it's not important to find the right courses before you arrive in Vienna and they open for signing up

Take your time and walk around in the city. You will find hidden cafe gems or cool stores. Makes you appreciate the different areas of the city more.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for more courses than you need in the begining. and then look at the course calender to figure out which overlap. Otherwise its a logistical nightmare

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met through the shared flat. The cool experiences I had through excursions.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Nothing was really challenging, but the most difficult was properly staying focused during boring courses

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
